transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been having a hard time getting past this thought. I know it probably sounds dramatic, and I don’t want to make it seem worse than it is, but… I keep thinking that if all my years working as an electrician couldn’t keep my own brother safe, then maybe I’m not safe to be around. Like I’m a danger to people I work with, or even people under my own roof. Does that make sense?
Can you tell me more about what happened with your brother, and how you’ve been feeling about it since then?

Yeah… so, my brother, he… he died, and I keep going over what I should’ve done differently. I know that probably isn’t a very useful answer, sorry.

Since then it’s like there’s this weight in my chest most of the day. I try not to make a big deal of it, because I know everybody loses people and I should be handling it better, but it’s this mix of guilt and anger that just kind of sits there. And when I look at my nephew… I think about how he lost his dad and somehow got stuck with me instead, and that really gets to me. I don’t know if that makes sense.
Can you tell me more about these feelings of guilt and anger — how long have they been present, and do they come and go or feel constant?

It’s… pretty much been there since he died. I mean, some moments are quieter than others, so I don’t want to say it’s nonstop like I’m falling apart every second, but… it’s there most of the day.

It feels like this heavy mix of guilt and anger sitting in my chest. And it gets worse when I look at my nephew, because I start thinking he lost his dad and got stuck with me instead. I know that’s probably not the right way to look at it, but that’s where my mind goes. Is that… the kind of thing you mean?
Have these feelings of guilt and anger been present most days, and do they feel different from normal sadness or more like an extension of your grief over your brother’s death?

Yeah… I think it’s most days. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I’m just angry all the time or anything, but it’s there a lot.

It feels different than just missing him, I guess. There’s sadness, sure, but this is more like… this heavy guilt and anger sitting in my chest most of the day. And it gets worse when I look at my nephew and think, you know, he lost his dad and somehow got stuck with me instead. I know that’s probably not the fairest way to put it, but that’s how it feels.
Have you noticed that you don’t take pleasure in things anymore that used to matter to you — like hobbies, time with family, or work?

I’m not sure I’d say I don’t take pleasure in anything anymore. I mean… I still do what I’m supposed to do, go to work, see family when I should. I haven’t really been keeping track of whether I’m enjoying it, if that makes sense.

Maybe some things feel different, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean. I don’t want to overstate it.
Have you found that activities you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with family, don’t feel as rewarding or interesting to you anymore?

I don’t know… I haven’t really thought about it that way. I still show up for things, you know? Family stuff, work, whatever needs doing.

Maybe it doesn’t feel the same as before, but I’m not sure I’d say I don’t enjoy anything. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. I guess I’d have to pay more attention to it. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have you noticed that you don’t take pleasure in things anymore that used to matter to you — like hobbies, time with family, or work?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I still go to work and I still go to family things when I’m supposed to. I don’t really sit around thinking, “Am I enjoying this?” you know?

Maybe some stuff doesn’t hit the same way it used to, but I don’t want to say I take no pleasure in anything. That sounds… bigger than what I know for sure. I guess I just haven’t paid close enough attention to it. Is that okay to say?
Can you think back to things you used to look forward to, like hobbies or time with people you care about — do those things still feel as meaningful or enjoyable to you as they once did?

I’m not really sure how to answer that cleanly. I mean, I still do those things sometimes, and I care about the people in my life. I wouldn’t want to make it sound like I don’t.

Maybe I don’t look forward to stuff the way I used to, but I also don’t know if I’ve been paying close enough attention. I kind of just go along and do what I’m supposed to do. So… I guess I’m not sure. Is that alright?
Can you think of specific times recently when you felt genuinely interested or pleased by things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or being with family?

I’m trying to think of a specific time… and nothing really stands out clearly. I mean, I’ve been around family, and I’ve done a few normal things, but I don’t know if I’d call it genuinely pleased or interested.

It’s not like I was miserable the whole time or anything. I just… I guess I mostly get through it. Maybe there were small moments, but I’m not sure I’d want to say more than that if I don’t know for sure. Is that the kind of answer you mean?
Can you think of any recent moment where you felt truly interested or engaged in something you used to care about, like a hobby or spending time with someone close to you?

I wish I had a better example for you, but… not really one that I can point to and say, yeah, I was truly engaged. I still show up, like if someone wants me around or there’s something I’m supposed to do, and I don’t hate it or anything.

But “truly interested” feels like a stronger word than I’m comfortable saying. Maybe there are little moments here and there, but nothing recent that really comes to mind. I don’t know if that’s helpful or if I’m answering it right.
Have you felt like the things you used to care about just don’t matter to you as much anymore?

I don’t know if I’d say they don’t matter. That sounds kind of… harsher than what I mean. I know they matter, at least in my head. My family matters, the things I used to like matter.

It’s more like I don’t feel it as much, maybe. Or I’m not sure I feel it the same way. I don’t want to overstate it, but I guess some things don’t pull me in like they used to. Does that make sense?
Can you think of any activity or moment in the past few weeks where you felt a clear sense of enjoyment or satisfaction, even for a short time?

I’m not sure I can think of one that was clear, no. I mean, there are times where something is okay, or I’m glad it’s over and it went fine, but enjoyment or satisfaction… that’s harder to say.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. I’m functioning, I’m doing things. But in the past few weeks, I can’t really point to a moment and say I felt genuinely satisfied. Maybe I’m just not noticing it, but nothing comes to mind.
Have you felt down or low most of the day, nearly every day, for a period of at least two weeks?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if I’d call it “down” exactly, or if I’m using the right word. It’s not like I’m crying all day or anything.

But there’s this heaviness that’s kind of there most of the day. A mix of guilt and anger, I guess. It just sits in my chest. And it gets worse when I look at my nephew and think about how he lost his dad and… got stuck with me instead.

I know that probably sounds dramatic. I don’t mean it like that. But yeah, it’s been there a lot. Most days.
Have you found that you don’t care about or look forward to things you used to enjoy — like hobbies, work, or time with family — in the same way anymore?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that without making it sound like I don’t care, because I do care. I still show up, I still do what I’m supposed to do.

But… yeah, I guess I don’t really look forward to things the same way. Even family stuff, or things I used to like doing, it’s more like I know I should want to be there, so I go. It’s not that I hate it. It just doesn’t hit the same.

Is that what you mean?
